content: Idempotency/exactly-once patterns across engines: nearly universal design is at-least-once execution + idempotent effect = effectively-exactly-once outcome (Temporal, Conductor state this explicitly). Workers/activities must tolerate duplicate delivery from network partitions, worker restarts, timeouts. Two implementation strategies: (1) pass a stable idempotency key to external APIs that support dedup (Stripe etc.), generated once and reused across retry attempts; (2) for owned databases, use conditional writes (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) or -- the strongest form -- make the step's DB write and the workflow's checkpoint/progress write part of the same transaction, which eliminates the need for any idempotency bookkeeping table. entflow's design (progress pointer + step effect in one tx for DB steps; framework-supplied deterministic key for Activities) matches the two best-practice patterns from both ends of the spectrum.
